To reduce power from the mods and to give more power to the community mod decisions could be repealed. Even If a mod created a subverse, it is the community that should really shape the direction of the sub.

I propose that if enough subscribers (a sizable proportion) flag a mod change for review, a voting 'card' is then sent to all the other subscriber's inboxes, or all subscribers that have been active on voat during the last seven days.

There should be three voting options, agree with mod, disagree with mod and no vote (if people don't reply in time this is also no vote). After 24hrs if there is a clear majority. For example if 70% of people, who voted, disagree with the mods decisions it would then be over turned.

There would be an automatic stickied post for 24hrs that would either be the removed post, an apology to the banned user or a post praising the mod if they are right. This would make the community aware of the results and give removed posts a fair chance or at least highlight the mods behavior.

I feel that the number of users needed to flag a mods decision should be quite high, so people can't abuse it. It should only have to be used when the community is genuinely in outrage.

I think this should only be implemented in subs over a certain size for obvious reasons.

If there was a mod rating system then this could feed in quite well, minus points for bad mod call and plus points if your community stands behind you.

This makes mods accountable to their community, not their ego. It could even be used to replace or introduce new mods. I would love to know your thoughts.
Subverse subscirbers should be able to overrule a mods decision with a majority voting system.
